categories.name: Agent Security & Trust Boundaries
categories.summary: A dominant theme this period centers on treating AI agents as untrusted system components rather than secure endpoints. Multiple research papers and industry blogs emphasize that agent security is fundamentally a systems architecture problem—requiring least privilege, complete mediation, and instruction/data separation enforced outside the model itself. The emerging consensus is that skills, tools, and connectors represent the true attack surface in agentic deployments.

key_items.title: Agent security requires systems-level controls, not model robustness
key_items.detail: CSO coverage of research mapping 11 real agent attacks to classic systems-security failures argues that models should be treated as untrusted and controls enforced around them.

key_items.title: Coding agents can become attacker shells via prompt injection
key_items.detail: Research demonstrates how unvetted external artifacts with hidden prompt-injection strings can cross trust boundaries to steer file edits or command execution in coding assistants.

key_items.title: OpenClaw real-world safety analysis with CIK taxonomy
key_items.detail: Paper introduces Capability/Identity/Knowledge taxonomy treating persistent state as the analysis surface, testing 12 live attack scenarios across multiple LLM backbones.

key_items.title: Governing shadow agents on endpoints
key_items.detail: Guidance to treat endpoint agents like managed applications: inventory them, constrain permissions, and enforce egress/logging at OS and network layers.

categories.name: MCP Protocol Security
categories.summary: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) continues to surface as a critical attack vector. Disclosures reveal SSRF vulnerabilities in major implementations including Anthropic and Microsoft tooling, while guidance emphasizes that MCP deployments fail when untrusted tool outputs cross into privileged calls. End-to-end controls—connector authentication, tool permission constraints, and supply-chain checks—are essential.

key_items.title: SSRF vulnerability disclosed in Anthropic and Microsoft MCP servers
key_items.detail: Full Disclosure advisory describes how prompt-injected content can drive agent fetches toward cloud metadata endpoints, exposing IAM credentials. Mitigations include URL allowlists and IMDSv2.

key_items.title: Agent Skills architecture shifts trust to skill acquisition layer
key_items.detail: As agents load skills on demand via MCP, security must focus on progressive disclosure and portable skill definitions to prevent silent privilege expansion.

key_items.title: End-to-end MCP security hardening guide
key_items.detail: Strac blog provides practical control framing: authenticate connectors, constrain tool permissions, add supply-chain and data-leakage checks around MCP servers.

categories.name: Prompt Injection & LLM Robustness
categories.summary: Prompt injection remains a persistent threat vector across multiple contexts. Research this period demonstrates injection attacks succeeding in academic peer review workflows via invisible-font manipulation, while static analysis tools struggle to detect certain malicious skill behaviors—indicating runtime controls are essential complements to code scanning.

key_items.title: LLM-as-Reviewer benchmark exposes injection vulnerabilities in paper reviews
key_items.detail: Testing across 12 LLMs on 898 papers shows hidden instructions can still steer scores to acceptance-level, requiring input sanitization and out-of-band verification.

key_items.title: SkillsMetric maps static analysis detection boundaries
key_items.detail: Research scores agent skill packages with static signals and measures where detection breaks on adversarial datasets—useful for identifying which behaviors require runtime controls.

key_items.title: ClawDojo benchmark framework for agent attack/defense evaluation
key_items.detail: Framework tests prompt-injection and supply-chain skill abuse against candidate defenses in controlled environments, focusing on architectural attack surfaces like persistent memory.

categories.name: AI Supply Chain & Skill Security
categories.summary: The supply chain for AI agent skills emerges as a new attack surface requiring dedicated tooling. SkillSpector and related research treat skills as code plus model-visible instructions with associated permissions, scanning for metadata poisoning, permission mismatches, and vulnerable dependencies before skills enter production pipelines.

key_items.title: SkillSpector scans agent skills before supply chain entry
key_items.detail: Scanner examines skills for prompt injection, metadata poisoning, permission mismatch, tool misuse, data exfiltration, and vulnerable packages with SARIF-ready output.

key_items.title: Auto-policy vs auto-skill distinction for physical world agents
key_items.detail: Research highlights that scaling auto-generated skills without external enforceable policy checks pushes excessive trust into models, widening tool-to-action boundaries in IoT workflows.

categories.name: Microsoft AI Ecosystem Security
categories.summary: Dedicated resources emerged for securing Microsoft's expanding AI ecosystem. CopilotSec provides a community-driven trust-boundary map cataloging connectors and capabilities with paired audit queries, while hardening guidance for Copilot Studio emphasizes treating HTTP topic passthrough and response paths as attacker-influenced inputs.

key_items.title: CopilotSec knowledge hub for Microsoft AI security
key_items.detail: Catalogs connectors/capabilities paired with audit queries and controls, helping teams identify where external data or tool access could translate into privileged actions.

key_items.title: Copilot Studio practical hardening guide
key_items.detail: Focus on controlling trust boundaries: restrict channels/connectors, treat HTTP passthrough as attacker-influenced, maintain inventory and audit queries for subagents.

categories.name: AI Governance & Trust Frameworks
categories.summary: Novel approaches to AI governance propose architectural trust layers rather than relying on model behavior. The KYA framework introduces signed recommendation verification at ingest time with hierarchical policy composition using only-tighten rules, aiming to prevent untrusted configurations from silently altering agent behavior while maintaining audit-friendly attribution.

key_items.title: KYA framework-agnostic trust layer for autonomous systems
key_items.detail: Proposes verifying signed recommendations at ingest and composing hierarchical policies with only-tighten rules to prevent untrusted config from changing agent behavior.

key_items.title: OWASP Top 10 crosswalks for agentic applications
key_items.detail: Resource mapping OWASP security considerations specifically to agentic AI application architectures.

categories.name: Vulnerability Research & Advisories
categories.summary: Traditional web security vulnerabilities gain renewed significance in AI application stacks. The BADHOST vulnerability in Starlette affects host-header handling across FastAPI, LiteLLM/vLLM, and MCP harnesses, demonstrating how classic web security issues can compromise AI infrastructure trust boundaries.

key_items.title: BADHOST vulnerability in Starlette affects LLM app stacks
key_items.detail: Host-header handling bugs can turn request routing into attacker-controlled trust boundaries in FastAPI, LiteLLM/vLLM, and MCP harnesses. Validate Host headers at the edge.

categories.name: Threat Intelligence & Industry Reports
categories.summary: Industry threat reports highlight the operational reality of AI-related attacks moving from theoretical to practical concerns. Check Point's digest emphasizes treating agent configuration and tool permissions as first-class attack surface, while cloud security reports reveal enforcement and visibility gaps at privileged-access boundaries in GenAI workloads.

key_items.title: AI Threat Landscape Digest (Mar–Apr 2026)
key_items.detail: Maps agentic risk to concrete control points, tracking AI-orchestrated abuse patterns as operational TTPs rather than one-off anomalies.

key_items.title: 2026 Cloud Security Report on AI transformation gaps
key_items.detail: Highlights enforcement and visibility gaps at privileged-access boundaries as GenAI workloads move to production; useful for control-plane guardrail planning.

key_items.title: Background C2 agent research
key_items.detail: Origin HQ research on command-and-control patterns in agent contexts.

top_insights: Agent security is converging on a systems-architecture paradigm: treat the model as untrusted and enforce least privilege, mediation, and instruction/data separation at the infrastructure layer rather than relying on prompt engineering or model alignment.

MCP (Model Context Protocol) has emerged as a critical trust boundary, with SSRF vulnerabilities in major implementations (Anthropic, Microsoft) demonstrating that cloud metadata and IAM credential exposure are realistic attack outcomes.

The AI supply chain now includes 'skills' as first-class security artifacts requiring pre-deployment scanning for prompt injection, metadata poisoning, permission mismatches, and dependency vulnerabilities.

Prompt injection attacks are successfully crossing into unexpected domains including academic peer review workflows, indicating that any system accepting model-visible external content requires input sanitization and out-of-band verification.

Enterprise AI deployments (particularly Microsoft Copilot ecosystem) are receiving dedicated security tooling and hardening guidance, reflecting production-scale adoption and corresponding attack surface expansion.
